title: MLS Commissioner would ‘love to see’ Liverpool’s Mohamed Salah in U.S.
content:
ATLANTA — MLS commissioner Don Garber believes outgoing Liverpool legend Mo Salah could make a significant impact in the top flight of American soccer, and has urged him to move to the U.S.

Speaking to reporters at the SBJ Business of Soccer event in Atlanta, Garber said he would “love to see (Salah) in our league”.

“I couldn’t say that until he announced that he was leaving Liverpool,” Garber said. “But what a great player he would be in MLS. And I think we would provide him with a great platform.”

Salah will be a free agent this summer and will surely receive interest from several countries around the world. At 33, his options may be limited, but given his global stature as a Premier League great, the Egyptian is likely to elicit interest from leagues willing to spend on a marquee name.

That is the modus operandi of the Saudi Pro League and MLS. Both leagues may soon be in a sweepstakes-like battle for his signature. MLS is currently experiencing a recruiting boom for international players over the age of 30 who can elevate the brand strength of the league and its respective clubs. Lionel Messi tops the list of recent signings.

Since joining Inter Miami in 2023, Messi has been joined in MLS by Rodrigo De Paul, another Argentine World Cup winner. Uruguayan legend Luis Suarez also plays for Miami. Former Tottenham Hotspur star Son Heung-min arrived last summer and has hit the ground running with title contenders LAFC. Vancouver signed former Germany international Thomas Müller and reached the 2025 MLS Cup final, losing to Messi and Miami.

Colombia captain James Rodriguez signed a six-month deal with Minnesota United in February. And this week, Orlando City announced that Atletico Madrid and France striker Antoine Griezmann will join the MLS side this summer. One can assume that Salah will take note of these recent signings and consider MLS an option for his next chapter.

“Obviously, if he (Salah) ever decides to come to Major League Soccer, we’d welcome him with open arms,” Garber said in December. “I’d say he should reach out to Leo (Messi) and reach out to Thomas Muller and see how happy they’ve been and how successful they’ve been and how much they’ve really embraced being in Major League Soccer.”

In July of 2027, MLS will switch to a spring-summer calendar in order to align its calendar with international soccer leagues around the world. That shift should help MLS teams take bigger swings in the global transfer market. The priority for team sporting directors is to attract players in their prime, rather than relying on over-age signings. But there will always be an appetite for big stars with massive international followings. Salah fits the bill.

“(The calendar change) is one piece of the puzzle,” Garber said on Wednesday. “Not having to think about selling your best players right before the playoffs is another part of it. Not having your playoffs compete with football, whether it’s college football or it’s the NFL as a part of it. If we want to be a major player on the global stage, we’ve got to play the same game the rest of the world’s playing, even if it’s a little harder for us.”

In MLS there could be several clubs that take an interest in Salah. Both Chicago Fire and New York City FC will open new soccer-specific stadiums; Chicago in 2028 and NYCFC in 2027. Salah would be a high-profile signing for either club.

NYCFC CEO Brad Sims was asked if the club needed to sign a big-name player to align with the new stadium’s opening.

“I don’t think we need that,” he said. “Would it be helpful? Of course. I think the direction the league is going in is really exciting, with the change in calendar aligning with the top leagues in the world. That will bring more opportunity and more interest in major signings across the league.

“So, is it a non-negotiable?” Sims continued. “Do we absolutely need it? In my opinion, no. Will it help take our club to the next level? Yes. I mean, I would love to have Mo Salah. We have not had any discussions with him or his people.”

San Diego FC, a team that played its first season in MLS in 2025, is owned by Egyptian-born billionaire Sir Mohamed Mansour, may be a popular alternative for Salah. However, The Athletic’s Tom Bogert reported on Tuesday that no active talks have taken place between Salah and the club. Chicago has not held talks with Salah either, per The Athletic.
